OR % 03.12.2024 CM APPL. 57154/2024 (on behalf of Local Commissioner Seeking directions)
1.

Ms. Swathi Sukumar, Senior Advocate and the Local Commissioner appointed by this Court, seeks directions to relocate Mr. Rohan Podar to the residential facility at Shaurya Foundation, Palwal,
Haryana.
Pursuant to the Court's previous order, Mr. Ravi Gupta, Senior Advocate and founder of Shaurya Foundation, is present before the Court.
Shaurya Foundation Trust

Mr.
Gupta apprised the Court of the facilities available at their institution.

He began by stating that the facility fosters a strong sense of community, where approximately 30 to 35 children and individuals with special needs are supported by a staff trained to address their specific requirements.
He further Vinod Kumar Poddar & Anr vs Local Level Committee Through Dc South ...

1 explained that the management ensures the well-being of residents by adhering to all necessary regulations concerning food safety and other standards.
The institution has an on-site medical facility, and a hospital is located just five minutes away.
Mr. Gupta added that, rather than providing formal education, they focus on skilling individuals through vocational training.

Moreover, music,
sports, and other activities form an integral part of the daily routine set for the residents.
2. In response to the Court's query, Mr. Gupta submits that the facility requires approximately three to four days to assess the special needs of any individual intending to reside there.
He has offered to take Mr. Rohan Podar under the care of the foundation, assuring the Court that this option would be in the best interest of Mr. Rohan Podar.
3. Mr. A. K. Chauhan, counsel for Respondent No.3 and the intervenor, strongly opposes the application.
He submits that Mr. Rohan Podar has lived in the house, set up by his father for a long period of time and relocating him would be catastrophic for Mr. Rohan Podar's well-being.
He also draws the attention of this Court to Section 10 of the National Trust for the Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation, and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999.

sentences.text: Section 10 of the Act outlines the objectives of the National Trust, which inter-alia include (a) To enable and empower persons This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 27/12/2024 at 22:04:45 with disabilities to live as independently and as fully as possible within and as close to the community to which they belong; (b) To strengthen facilities to provide support to persons with disabilities to live within their own families.
4. Counsel for the Petitioners, on the other hand, submits that the Petitioners just want Mr. Rohan Podar's safety and well-being and would like for him to live with the Petitioners.
5. Counsel for Respondent No.1 submits that they have no objection to the request made in this application.
6. The Court has given thoughtful consideration to the submissions of all parties and the circumstances surrounding the care and well-being of Mr. Rohan Podar, a young man with special needs.
The unfortunate and untimely demise of his father, Mr. Sunil Podar, has undeniably left a profound void in Rohan's life--both emotionally and in terms of his living arrangements.

This loss has not only deprived him of his primary caregiver and source of emotional support but has also disrupted the structured environment that revolved around his father's presence and involvement.
Presently, Rohan resides alone in the home established by his late father, with only caretaking staff for company.
While the dedication of the caretakers is acknowledged, their presence cannot replicate the nurturing environment of a family or a community.
Rohan's interactions are limited to these caretakers, confining his world to the four walls of his residence.
Such isolation may impede his social development and emotional well-being, particularly given his special needs.

Furthermore,
the Court notes with concern that serious allegations have been exchanged between the parties who have applied for guardianship of Rohan.
While the veracity of these This is a digitally signed order.

The potential for conflict and instability necessitates a neutral and supportive environment to safeguard his well-being.
The paramount consideration for this Court is the welfare and best interests of Rohan.
The Court's deliberations are guided by the need to ensure that he is placed in an environment that fosters his physical, emotional, and social development.
7. The Shaurya Foundation, as presented by Mr. Ravi Gupta, Senior Advocate and founder of the institution, embodies these principles.

A community-oriented setting, such as that offered by Shaurya Foundation, presents an opportunity for Rohan to engage socially, form friendships,
acquire new skills, and benefit from a structured routine.
Such an environment can significantly enhance his quality of life by promoting inclusivity and personal growth.
It aligns with contemporary approaches to care for individuals with special needs, emphasizing integration and empowerment.
Furthermore, Mr. Gupta's commitment is both professional and personal, with his own son residing at the facility.
The Foundation specializes in empowering individuals with developmental disabilities through vocational training, sports, music, and other enriching activities.
It provides a safe, nurturing environment staffed by trained professionals capable of addressing Rohan's specific needs.
The Medical Board's assessment dated 19th May 2024 corroborates the necessity of such an environment.
It has been opined that Rohan requires assistance with daily activities like eating and bathing and communicates minimally through non- verbal cues.
These findings highlight the importance of placing him in a setting where he can receive comprehensive care and opportunities for social This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 27/12/2024 at 22:04:46 interaction and skill development.

8. This Court has also considered the objections raised by Mr. A.K. Chauhan, counsel for Respondent No. 3.
9.
In the absence of any blood relatives to assume responsibility for Rohan's care, the Court is placed in the challenging position of making a critical decision about his future.
The Court is acutely aware that this is not an easy call to make.
Intervening in the life of a vulnerable individual, particularly one with special needs, demands utmost sensitivity and caution.
The Court recognizes the profound impact that relocating Rohan from his familiar home environment may have on his emotional and psychological well-being.
The comfort and familiarity of his current surroundings, established by his late father, cannot be understated.
Thus, the Court must thus balance the inherent risks and benefits of relocation.

Remaining isolated in his current residence may limit Rohan's opportunities for social engagement, personal development, and access to specialized care that could significantly improve his quality of life.
Conversely, integrating into a community like the Shaurya Foundation could provide him with a nurturing environment tailored to his needs.

sentences.text: The Court does not doubt the intentions of any parties involved; however, it's decision cannot be swayed by external interests or conflicts.
The guiding principle must be the welfare of Rohan.

In making this difficult decision, the Court is guided by the objectives outlined in the National Trust Act, 1999, which emphasizes enabling persons with disabilities to live as independently and fully as possible within a supportive community.
Mr. Gupta's personal commitment to the cause, evidenced by his own son's residence at the facility, provides additional assurance of the level of care This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 27/12/2024 at 22:04:46 and dedication that Rohan would receive.
Therefore, the Court believes that relocating Rohan to the residential facility at Shaurya Foundation, Palwal, Haryana, is in his best interest.
11. However, recognizing the significance of this transition, the Court deems it appropriate to proceed with caution.
An initial assessment period will allow all parties to evaluate Rohan's adaptability to the new environment and ensure that his specific needs are adequately met.
This measured approach balances the need for decisive action with the responsibility to safeguard Rohan's welfare.
12. In view of the foregoing, the Court issues the following directions:

(a) The Local Commissioner is authorized to relocate Mr. Rohan Podar to the residential facility at Shaurya Foundation, Palwal, for a few days, for the initial assessment, at a time and date coordinated with Mr. Ravi Gupta, Senior Advocate.
(b) The Local Commissioner shall coordinate with Mr. Hanumant Rawat, who shall drop Rohan at the residential facility.
Any out-of-pocket expenses incurred for transportation shall be reimbursed, upon submission of the costs to this Court, with appropriate directions issued on the next date of hearing.
(c) As per the fee schedule of Shaurya Foundation, the assessment fee for the duration (2 nights and 3 days) is INR 6,000/-.
HDFC Bank, Safdarjung Enclave, is directed to pay INR 6,000/- to Shaurya Foundation from late Mr. Sunil Podar's HDFC Account No. 05031930003403 by Demand Draft, which shall be an interim payment.
(d) It is clarified that, necessary directions as regards the payment for Rohan's stay in the residential facility, over and above the aforenoted period, if any, shall be issued on the next date.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

4

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (e) All parties, including Mr. Hanumant and the current caretaking staff of Rohan, are directed to facilitate the smooth transition from Rohan's current residence to Shaurya Foundation, Palwal, on the date of relocation.

(f) The Local Commissioner is directed to coordinate with Shaurya Foundation and Mr. Ravi Gupta and file an assessment report regarding Rohan's adaptability and well-being at the residential facility before the next date of hearing.

13. The Court urges all parties involved to cooperate fully and place Rohan's welfare above all other considerations and remain committed to ensuring that Rohan receives the care and support he deserves.
14. For further directions, list on 18th December, 2024.

In light of the fact that this Court is considering the issues which have a bearing on the guardianship of Mr. Rohan Podar, till the next date of hearing, Respondent No.1 is directed to maintain status quo as regards the guardianship applications filed with respect to him.
16. Renotify on 18th December, 2024.
SANJEEV NARULA, J DECEMBER 3, 2024 d.negi

(b) The Local Commissioner shall coordinate with Mr. Hanumant Rawat, who shall drop Rohan at the residential facility.

(c) As per the fee schedule of Shaurya Foundation, the assessment fee for the duration (2 nights and 3 days) is INR 6,000/-.
